title: Rate Lock Commitment Dispute Standard
content:
**Rate Lock Commitment disputes filed by borrowers.**

### Filing window

A lock dispute is accepted only if it is filed no later than the end of the dispute window that started on the disputed event.

- For a lock request or rate dispute, the window counts business days forward from the lock's lock date, which is day zero.
- For an extension or relock dispute, it counts from the disputed pricing entry's entry date, which is day zero.

Filing on the last business day of the window is on time. A business day is Monday through Friday, excluding the US federal public holidays observed by the Federal Reserve Banks. Saturdays, Sundays and those holidays are skipped when counting. The window length is the product's dispute filing window, and the anchor dates are read from the lock's records.

A late dispute is resolved as denied as untimely.

| Filed on (business days after day zero) | With a 10-business-day window |
|---|---|
| Business day 10 | On time |
| Business day 11 | Late: denied as untimely |

*Hypothetical illustration:* if day zero is a Monday and no holiday falls in the next two weeks, business day 10 is the Friday of the following week. A filing on that Friday is on time. A filing on the next Monday is late.

### Decision time

The lock desk decides within the product's decision time in business days.

### Lock request and wrong-rate disputes

For a dispute that a lock request was not honored, or that the wrong rate was locked, the claim is honored on the claimed terms only when all of the following hold:

- the lock request log holds a request of the type initial lock or relock for this lock;
- that request is dated on the claimed request date, at the claimed rate;
- it was time-stamped no later than the lock desk cutoff time on a business day;
- the loan file was in one of the lock's eligible loan file statuses that day.

The lock is then repriced to the claimed rate, at that request's rate-sheet price plus the term price adjustment, keeping the expiration date.

A matching request time-stamped after the cutoff is resolved as denied after the cutoff, because it was correctly priced on the next business day. No matching request is resolved as denied for no record. An email or call that the log does not show does not count.

| What the log shows | Outcome |
|---|---|
| Matching request on or before the cutoff on a business day, file status eligible that day | Honored on the claimed terms |
| Matching request time-stamped after the cutoff | Denied after the cutoff |
| No matching request | Denied for no record |

### Extension charge disputes

*Clause no longer in force:* the former clause on extension charge disputes is no longer in force and has been superseded by the current basis for deciding them. It provided that the charged extension is waived (extension cost waived) only when the appraisal-delay case of the extension policy covers it, and that otherwise the dispute is denied as borrower caused.

### Relock pricing disputes

*Clause no longer in force:* the former clause on relock pricing disputes is no longer in force and has been superseded by the current basis for relock pricing. It provided that relock pricing disputes are upheld only when the relock price is worse than the worst-case rule allows, by repricing to the rule's result.

### Record of the decision

Every decision names the filing record, and the matched request where one exists.

superseded_clauses: For an extension_charge_disputed dispute, the charged extension is waived (extension_cost_waived) only when the appraisal-delay case of the extension policy covers it; otherwise it is denied_borrower_caused.
relock_pricing_disputed disputes are upheld only when the relock price is worse than the worst-case rule allows, by repricing to the rule's result.
